speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I understand you have progressive swelling and pain in your right ring finger. To help me narrow down the cause, how long has this been going on, and has the pain been constant or does it come and go?

speaker: Patient
text: 22-year-old male. The patient reports that the pain and swelling in his right ring finger began 2 days ago while playing football. He recalls his finger got caught in the jersey of another player, who then pulled away forcefully.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Traumatic Arthritis (Post-traumatic joint injury).

The history of the finger getting caught and forcefully pulled during football suggests an acute traumatic event leading to joint damage. Given the rapid onset (2 days) of swelling and pain following a clear mechanism of injury, this is most consistent with a traumatic arthritis or severe soft tissue injury rather than an infectious process like septic arthritis, which typically presents more gradually.

DIAGNOSIS_READY_Answer: Rupture of the flexor digitorum profundus tendon at its point of insertion
